In [[mathematics]], '''rank-finiteness for fusion categories''' is a collection of related [[theorem]]s and [[conjecture]]s about structures related to [[Fusion category|fusion categories]]. The question is whether or not a given categorical structure related to fusion categories has [[Finite set|finitely]] many or [[Infinite set|infinitely]] many equivalence classes of a given rank. The original result in this direction was Ocneanu rigidity, which asserts that every fusion ring has finitely many [[categorification]]s.<ref name="g984">{{cite journal |last=Kitaev |first=Alexei |author-link=Alexei Kitaev |year=2006 |title=Anyons in an exactly solved model and beyond |journal=Annals of Physics |publisher=Elsevier BV |volume=321 |issue=1 |pages=2–111 |arxiv=cond-mat/0506438 |bibcode=2006AnPhy.321....2K |doi=10.1016/j.aop.2005.10.005 |issn=0003-4916 |doi-access=free}}</ref> A particularly relevant example to [[condensed matter physics]] is the rank-finiteness theorem for [[Modular tensor category|modular tensor categories]].<ref>Rank-finiteness and the nature of the universe, by PAUL BRUILLARD, SIU-HUNG NG, ERIC C. ROWELL, AND ZHENGHAN WANG

https://aimath.org/wp-content/uploads/Authors-Account-2019.pdf</ref><ref name=":13">{{Citation |last1=Bruillard |first1=Paul |title=Rank-finiteness for modular categories |date=2013-10-01 |journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society |volume=29 |issue=3 |pages=857–881 |url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013arXiv1310.7050B/abstract |access-date=2025-02-22 |arxiv=1310.7050 |doi=10.1090/jams/842 |last2=Ng |first2=Siu-Hung |last3=Rowell |first3=Eric C. |last4=Wang |first4=Zhenghan}}</ref>

Here and throughout, the rank of a fusion category refers to the number of isomorphism classes of simple objects it has.

== Ocneanu rigidity ==
The '''Ocneanu rigidity''' theorem, named after mathematician Adrian Ocneanu, asserts that every fusion ring has finitely many [[categorification]]s. Stated more directly, this means that are only finitely many equivalence classes of [[Fusion category|fusion categories]] with a given set of fusion rules. The braided version of Ocneanu rigidity states that there are only finitely many equivalence classes of [[Braided monoidal category|braided]] fusion categories with a given set of fusion rules.<ref name="g984" />

The proof of Ocneanu rigidity relies on the demonstrating vanishing of the Davydov-Yetter cohomology groups, which classify certain equivalence classes of deformations of fusion categories.<ref>{{cite journal |arxiv=1910.06094 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2022.108853 |title=Davydov-Yetter cohomology, comonads and Ocneanu rigidity |date=2023 |last1=Gainutdinov |first1=Azat M. |last2=Haferkamp |first2=Jonas |last3=Schweigert |first3=Christoph |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=414 |article-number=108853 }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Etingof |first1=Pavel |author-link1=Pavel Etingof |last2=Nikshych |first2=Dmitri |last3=Ostrik |first3=Viktor |date=2005-09-01 |title=On fusion categories |url=https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2005.162.581 |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=162 |issue=2 |pages=581–642 |doi=10.4007/annals.2005.162.581 |issn=0003-486X}}</ref>

== Positive results on rank finiteness ==
There are several known cases of rank-finiteness. These

* The rank-finiteness theorem for [[modular tensor category]] is a theorem due to Paul Bruillard, Siu-Hung Ng, Eric Rowell, and [[Zhenghan Wang]].<ref name=":13" />
* The rank-finiteness theorem for [[Braided monoidal category|braided]] fusion categories is a theorem due to Corey Jones, Scott Morrison, Dmitri Nikshych, and Eric Rowell.<ref name=":1">{{cite journal
| arxiv=1902.06165
| last1=Jones | first1=Corey
| last2=Morrison | first2=Scott
| last3=Nikshych | first3=Dmitri
| last4=Rowell | first4=Eric C.
| title=Rank-finiteness for G-crossed braided fusion categories
| date=2021 
| journal=Transformation Groups
| volume=26
| pages=915–927
| doi=10.1007/s00031-020-09576-2}}</ref>
* The rank-finiteness theorem for G-crossed braided fusion categories is a theorem, also due to Jones et al.<ref name=":1" />
* The rank-finiteness theorem for super-modular tensor categories is a theorem, also due to Jones et al.<ref name=":1" />

== Unknown results on rank finiteness ==
It is not known whether or not there are finitely many fusion categories of a given rank. Similarly, it is not known whether or not there are finitely many [[Pivotal category|pivotal]] fusion categories and [[Spherical category|spherical]] fusion categories of a given rank. This is related to the other open problem of determining whether or not it is true that every fusion category admits a pivotal (or even spherical) structure.<ref name=":0" />
